Africa CDC notes the Bundibugyo outbreak is larger than the 2007 and 2012 outbreaks, and there are currently no approved vaccines or treatments for this strain.

triage.headline_ja: WHO、アフリカCDC、コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ感染症への対応に5億1800万ドルの計画を発表
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4つ全て該当。エボラ出血熱の確認された多国間アウトブレイク（DRC 381例64死亡、ウガンダ16例1死亡）で、公衆衛生への深刻な影響、予想外の大規模性（過去の同類型アウトブレイクより大きい）、国際的拡大（ウガンダに波及）、ワクチン・治療法の欠如による国際関心が極めて高い。
triage.notes: ウガンダはAPI発生地域に含まれるが、記事サマリーの対象国リストに未含。DRCのみ verified_locations に計上。Bundibugyo株は過去の2007年・2012年のアウトブレイクより規模が大きく、ワクチン・承認治療法なしという極めて高いリスク。WHO・Africa CDCの大規模対応計画（5.18億ドル）も社会的・政治的関心の高さを示唆。

article.articleHeadline: Světová zdravotnická organizace oznámila půlroční plán boje proti epidemii eboly
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: World Health Organization announced a six-month plan to combat the Ebola epidemic.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and neighboring Uganda is addressed by a six-month WHO plan worth $518 million to stop transmission and prepare other nations. WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus announced the package in Nairobi/Kinshasa, stressing border controls and sustained political and financial commitment as essential. The outbreak has reached 381 confirmed cases and 62 deaths in the DRC; Uganda reports 19 cases and two deaths. The Bundibugyo variant is circulating in both countries, for which there is no vaccine or effective treatment; some Ebola strains have vaccines and medicines. The CDC notes the epidemic was overlooked for weeks, complicating containment. Ebola spreads by contact with an infected person or contaminated materials and causes fever, vomiting, diarrhea, muscle pain, and bleeding. No imported or exported cases are detailed.

triage.headline_ja: 世界保健機関がエボラ流行との戦いの6ヶ月計画を発表
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4つすべてに該当（深刻な公衆衛生影響、異常な発生、国際的拡大リスク、渡航制限リスク）。DRCとウガンダでの確認事例と死亡例があり、WHOによる大規模対応計画が既に発表されている。
triage.notes: 記事はDRCにおけるエボラ流行の主要な発生地を明確に述べており、ウガンダでの事例も報告されているが、ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれていないため除外。ナイロビはWHO会議開催地として言及されているが、発生地ではないため除外。ワクチンや有効な治療法がないBundibugyo亜型が循環している点が重大。

article.articleHeadline: منظمة الصحة العالمية: 518 مليون دولار لمكافحة إيبولا
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: World Health Organization: $518 million to combat Ebola
article.articleSummary: World Health Organization and Africa CDC launched a joint plan worth $518 million to tackle the Ebola outbreak that is prompting concern in the Democratic Republic of Congo and neighboring countries. The plan, running June through November, follows the outbreak declared May 15 in northeastern DRC, with the Bundibugyo ebolavirus lineage suspected in circulation. As of the latest WHO data, 381 confirmed infections in DRC and 64 deaths. The outbreak spans three provinces, with Ituri province identified as the epicenter, accounting for about 90% of confirmed cases and 76% of deaths. Across the border in northeastern Uganda, there have been 16 confirmed cases and one death. WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said the plan focuses on emergency coordination, surveillance, laboratory testing, infection prevention, outbreak control, clinical care, and community engagement. There are no licensed vaccines or approved therapeutics for Bundibugyo ebolavirus. The outbreak is larger than past Bundibugyo outbreaks.

triage.headline_ja: 世界保健機関：エボラ対策に5億1800万ドル
triage.triage_reason: エボラウイルス病のアウトブレイクで、DRCおよびウガンダで確認された事例が存在し、IHR基準2つ以上（重篤性、異常性、国際的拡大リスク）に該当。WHO が大規模資金投入を決定するなど社会政治的関心が高い。
triage.notes: 記事サマリーでウガンダ（GeoNames ID: 226074）にも16確認例と1死亡が記述されているが、ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations に含めない。DRCはリストに含まれるため計上。Bundibugyo ebolavirus は既知のエボラウイルスだが、過去のアウトブレイクより規模が大きいとされており、ワクチン・治療薬がないため管理上の困難がある。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola - Des experts de la santé appellent à une trêve humanitaire pour lutter contre Ebola
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola - Health experts call for a humanitarian truce to fight Ebola
article.articleSummary: Two health experts, including Emmanuel André and Erika Vlieghe, called on Friday for a temporary humanitarian truce to fight the Ebola outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo. The outbreak is caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus and was deemed a Public Health Emergency of International Concern by the World Health Organization in late May, though the true scale remains uncertain. In North Kivu and Ituri provinces, insecurity has displaced over 2 million people, hindering access to care and increasing transmission risk. Logistical and security challenges impede patient transfers, staffing, and supply lines. The experts warn that rapid response is critical and argue that a humanitarian pause would enable safer, faster patient management, movement of personnel, and deployment of equipment to curb further spread.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ - 保健専門家がエボラ対策のための人道的休戦を呼びかけ
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4項目全て該当（深刻な公衆衛生影響、予想外の大規模アウトブレイク、国際拡大リスク、渡航制限リスク）。WHO PHEIC指定済みの確認されたエボラアウトブレイク。
triage.notes: WHO PHEIC指定済みの確認されたエボラアウトブレイク（Bundibugyo ebolavirus）。北キブ州およびイトゥリ州で200万人以上が避難。セキュリティと物流の課題により対応が著しく阻害されている。この記事は人道的休戦の呼びかけであり、既知の重篤な状況の進展を示す。

article.articleHeadline: South Africa: Cabinet Outlines Action On Drugs, Ebola Preparedness
article.articleSummary: Cabinet reaffirmed commitment to fighting organized crime and continental Ebola preparedness. Security authorities intercepted at Beitbridge Port of Entry on 27 May 2026 a truck travelling through Zimbabwe into South Africa carrying about 713,000 g of methaqualone (ABBA), linked to Mandrax manufacture, in a shipment valued at nearly R1 billion; 11 suspects were arrested, including four Mexican nationals, after discovery of a Swartruggens farm drug-lab in North West. On health, SA contributed US$5 million to a continental Ebola preparedness and response plan within a US$319 million African initiative to address outbreaks in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda. WHO declared Ebola a PHEIC; Cabinet stresses no alarm in SA, as Ebola is not endemic here and transmission requires direct contact with bodily fluids. Monitoring and regional collaboration continue.

triage.headline_ja: 南アフリカ：内閣が薬物対策とエボラ準備態勢に関する行動を概説
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱は確認されたPHEICだが、サマリーから南アフリカではエボラ症例が報告されておらず、準備態勢と資金貢献に関する記事である。DRCとウガンダの流行への地域的対応についての報道。
triage.notes: 発生地域にはDRC、ウガンダ、南アフリカ、ジンバブエが含まれているが、サマリーの主題はDRCとウガンダでのエボラ流行である。南アフリカの記事だが、南アフリカ国内でのエボラ症例報告はなく、準備態勢と資金貢献が主体。対象国リストに含まれるのはDRCのみ。WHOがPHEICを宣言済みで公開性が高いが、南アフリカ国内での発生ではないため、シグナル昇格には至らないと判断。

article.articleHeadline: WHO announces $518 million six-month plan to fight Ebola
article.articleSummary: On 2026-06-05, the World Health Organization launched a $518 million six-month plan (June–November 2026) to fight Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo, targeting the Bundibugyo strain—the fourth-largest Bundibugyo outbreak on record and Congo's 17th Ebola outbreak. Congo has reported 381 confirmed cases and 62 deaths. The Bundibugyo strain has no approved treatment or vaccine; vaccines and therapies are under development. Africa CDC said the outbreak persisted for weeks undetected, leaving authorities behind and complicating containment. Donors pledged about $315.8 million toward containment, down from an initial $498 million; it was not clear whether those funds will be allocated to the six-month plan. The outbreak on May 15 was declared a public health emergency of international concern by WHO. Containment requires political commitment, sustained financing, and trust-building with communities.

triage.headline_ja: WHO、エボラ熱対策に5億1800万ドルの6ヶ月計画を発表
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4項目全て該当。コンゴ民主共和国でのエボラ出血熱（Bundibugyo株）は死亡率を伴う重篤な感染症で、公衆衛生上の国際的関心事項（PHEIC宣言済み）であり、国際支援の必要性が明白。
triage.notes: エボラウイルス病（Bundibugyo株）はコンゴ民主共和国で発生。381確定患者、62名死亡。治療法とワクチンが未承認の状況。WHOによりPHEIC宣言済み（2026年5月15日）。6ヶ月間の対策に多額の国際支援が必要とされている。

article.articleHeadline: خطة طارئة لمكافحة إيبولا بـ518 مليون دولار.. هل تنجح في احتواء الوباء؟ - صحيفة الوئام
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: An $518 million emergency plan to combat Ebola: will it succeed in containing the outbreak?
article.articleSummary: WHO, in collaboration with Africa CDC, launched a US$518 million emergency plan to curb an Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and neighboring countries. The plan runs June–November 2026 and focuses on rapid response, enhanced epidemiological surveillance, laboratory capacity, infection prevention and control, clinical care, and broader community engagement. The outbreak, declared May 15 in northeast DRC, is caused by the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, for which no licensed vaccines or treatments exist. As of the latest WHO update, there are 381 confirmed cases and 64 deaths in DRC across three provinces, with Ituri Province accounting for about 90% of confirmed infections and 76% of fatalities. The outbreak has extended to Uganda, reporting 16 confirmed cases and one death so far, raising regional containment concerns. The plan provides a concrete, time-bound framework to contain transmission and prevent wider spread.

triage.headline_ja: $518百万ドルの緊急計画でエボラ熱対策へ：封じ込めに成功するか？
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱の確認された多数の症例と死亡、地域的な拡大、国際的対応の組織化が認められ、IHR基準2つ以上およびWPRO基準複数に該当。国際的支援体制の構築が進行中の緊急事態。
triage.notes: ウガンダ（226074）は発生地域として含まれているが、記事サマリーでは「neighboring countries」および16確認症例と1死亡の言及のみで、DRCが主要な発生地であり、ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれていないため、verified_locationsからは除外した。エボラ出血熱（Bundibugyo株）による確認症例381例、死亡64例（DRC）という深刻な公衆衛生上の影響と、WHOおよびAfrica CDCによる$518百万規模の国際的対応体制の立ち上げが確認された。

article.articleHeadline: Вспышку Эболы в Африке признали четвертой по масштабу
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ebola outbreak in Africa was recognized as the fourth largest.
article.articleSummary: As of 5 June 2026, the Ebola outbreak in Africa, centered in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and Uganda, is the fourth largest and most severe since 1976, according to the Africa CDC. The current outbreak has 381 confirmed cases and 65 deaths. It ranks behind the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic (28,616 cases, 11,325 deaths), the 2018–2020 eastern DRC outbreak (3,470 cases, 2,287 deaths), and the 2000–2001 Uganda outbreak (425 cases, 224 deaths). Across Africa, Ebola has caused more than 30 outbreaks with about 15,000 total deaths observed. The World Health Organization had previously declared the DRC outbreak a crisis and sought $115 million for the next three months; by publication, only about 35% of that funding was funded.

triage.headline_ja: アフリカのエボラ出血熱流行が過去4番目の規模として認識される
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4項目すべてに該当。エボラ出血熱という高い致死率の感染症で、複数国での確認、国際的拡大リスク、死亡者と多数の患者が報告されている。
triage.notes: Bluedot APIの発生地域にはウガンダとアンゴラも含まれているが、記事サマリーでは発生地がDRC及びウガンダに集中していると記載されている。しかし対象国リストではウガンダ(226074)は含まれていないため、verified_locationsはDRCのみとした。本件は高い優先度でフルRRA（Rapid Risk Assessment）に進める必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: NCDC on red alert, intensifies nationwide preparedness against possible Ebola outbreak
article.articleSummary: Nigeria's NCDC has intensified preparedness for Ebola importation amid an outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo and regional transmission to Uganda. There is currently no confirmed Ebola case in Nigeria, but the risk of importation of the Bundibugyo strain is high due to regional spread, travel, and porous borders. Nigeria has strengthened infection prevention and control at points of entry and ensured ready laboratories and health facilities. A comprehensive risk assessment classified states by mobility and border connectivity, with readiness completed in 549 health facilities across 32 states plus Federal Capital Territory, and 17 designated treatment centres assessed for screening, isolation, IPC, and capacity. National advisories disseminated, and a dynamic risk assessment guides the National Emergency Operations Centre. WHO declared PHEIC on May 17, 2026; Africa CDC declared PHECS on May 18, 2026. About 1,100 suspected Ebola and 263 confirmed with 43 deaths in DRC and Uganda.

triage.headline_ja: NCDC、赤色警報発令、エボラ出血熱の可能性に向けて全国的準備態勢を強化
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4項目すべてに該当する。DRC・ウガンダでのエボラ出血熱の流行があり、ナイジェリアへの輸入リスク高大で、国際的拡大・渡航制限の懸念が生じている。WHOがPHEIC、Africa CDCがPHECSを宣言済み。
triage.notes: DRCおよびウガンダでの流行が既に発生し、ナイジェリアはまだ確認症例なしだが輸入リスク高大。記事サマリーで具体的に記載されているのはDRC・ウガンダでの発生。対象国リストに含まれるのはDRCのみ。WHOがPHEIC宣言（2026年5月17日）、Africa CDCがPHECS宣言（2026年5月18日）済み。DRC・ウガンダで約1,100疑似症、263確認症例、43死亡。

article.articleHeadline: Samu capacita profissionais para atender casos suspeitos de ebola no Rio - Diário do Rio de Janeiro
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: SAMU trains professionals to respond to suspected Ebola cases in Rio de Janeiro.
article.articleSummary: Rio de Janeiro, Brazil — SAMU trained responders in biosafety for transporting patients with suspected Ebola, to protect patients, staff, and the public. The program, overseen by the State Health Secretariat (SES-RJ), covers PPE use (masks, face shields, gloves, impermeable gowns, and coveralls) and ambulance preparation and decontamination. Two ambulances, stationed in the city center and West Zone, were adapted for suspected high-consequence disease transport and follow international guidelines. The training, delivered by Instituto Nacional de Infectologia Evandro Chagas (Fiocruz), is part of a contingency plan integrating the Central Regulation, Inter-hospital Transport, and Pre-Hospital Control. The relevance was shown by a recent case: a patient from Uganda suspected of Ebola was transported to Fiocruz, but tests ruled out Ebola in favor of malaria. Brazil’s Health Ministry maintains a low transmission risk. CIS monitors Ebola alerts; 2025 had six worldwide occurrences; 2026 has 11 notifications as of 2026-06-05.

triage.headline_ja: SAMU がリオデジャネイロでエボラウイルス病の疑い例対応のための専門家養成を実施
triage.triage_reason: ブラジルはエボラウイルス病対応の準備態勢構築を示しており、ウガンダからの疑い例輸送が実際に発生したが、確定例は検出されていない。情報は現在のところ予防的準備段階であり、IHR基準2つ以上の該当は認められない。
triage.notes: 記事主題はブラジル（リオデジャネイロ）における予防的対応体制の構築である。ウガンダからの疑い例が言及されているが、この患者はブラジルに輸送されて検査を受けており、確定例ではなくマラリアと判明している。現在のところ確定されたエボラウイルス病患者は発生していない。スクリーニング基準では「異常/予想外」（新しい訓練プログラムの開始）および「流行しやすさ」（高リスク病原体への対応準備）に該当するが、WPROでの基準該当は2つにとどまる。社会的・政治的関心は高いが、実際の感染事例がないため、WATCH判定とした。今後の情報追跡が必要。

article.articleHeadline: WHO、エボラ対策に830億円　感染検査や患者との接触を追跡
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: WHO allocates 83 billion yen for Ebola countermeasures, including diagnostic testing and contact tracing.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease outbreak centered in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and extending to Uganda prompts a joint WHO–Africa CDC plan. A six-month response (June–November) targets expanded testing, contact tracing, and procurement of personal protective equipment, with a budget of $518 million (about ¥83 billion). The plan anticipates roughly 3,600 cases and will bolster testing and treatment in the DRC and Uganda, while aiding neighboring countries with surveillance and preparedness. Funding will come from affected nations, WHO, UNICEF, and partners, with calls for broader international support. WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus stresses rapid, coordinated action to halt transmission. Africa CDC reports 397 confirmed cases and 63 deaths as of June 3. The initiative aims to curb the outbreak through lab confirmation, case management, and containment across affected and neighboring states.

triage.headline_ja: WHO、エボラ対策に830億円　感染検査や患者との接触を追跡
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4つすべてに該当。エボラウイルス感染症は公衆衛生上の深刻な影響、異常性、複数国への国際的拡大、渡航・貿易制限のリスクを有する。WPROスクリーニング基準でも全項目に該当。
triage.notes: ウガンダは記事サマリーに言及されているが、対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations から除外。DRCはリスト内で該当。397確認症例、63死亡（6月3日時点）。WHO・Africa CDCによる6ヶ月対応計画が進行中。

article.articleHeadline: Нынешняя вспышка лихорадки Эбола в Африке стала четвертой по масштабу
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The current Ebola outbreak in Africa has become the fourth largest in scale.
article.articleSummary: As of June 5, 2026, the current Ebola outbreak in Africa ranks as the fourth largest since 1976. Historical totals cited: West Africa (2014–2016) with 28,616 cases and 11,325 deaths; East Congo (2018–2020) with 3,470 cases and 2,287 deaths; Uganda (2000–2001) with 425 cases and 224 deaths. The new outbreak began with first reports on May 5 from Ituri Province, Democratic Republic of the Congo, and the WHO later declared it a public health emergency of international concern. The eastern Congo outbreak has expanded into new districts amid armed conflict, reaching 22 health zones across three provinces. Russian health official Anna Popova states that Ebola is a contact infection, not transmitted via airborne droplets, and therefore does not have pandemic potential.

triage.headline_ja: アフリカの現在のエボラ出血熱の流行は規模において4番目となった
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4項目すべてに該当。エボラ出血熱は重篤な公衆衛生上の影響を持ち、国際的な懸念の公衆衛生上の緊急事態として宣言されており、複数国への拡大リスクと国際的な感染症対応が必要とされている。
triage.notes: DRCのイトゥリ州で2026年5月5日に初報が確認された現在のエボラ流行について。WHOが国際的な公衆衛生上の緊急事態を宣言している。記事では東コンゴの流行が複数州と保健地域に拡大していることが示されており、武装紛争に伴う対応上の課題も存在する。ロシアの保健当局は空気感染リスクがないと指摘しているが、接触感染による拡大リスクは存在する。

article.articleHeadline: Should I hug my children? Ebola doctor on outbreak frontlines faces daily dilemma
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in eastern DRC's Ituri province, including Bunia. Dr. Patrick Katabuka, 45, drives village to village, collecting samples and coordinating transport to centers. Only one Ebola treatment center is operating at standard capacity; others are unfinished. Ongoing conflict in Ituri blocks access to communities, hindering case detection and contact tracing. Protective equipment is scarce and hot; lab results can take more than three days. Inside centers, suspected patients—often children and mothers—wait separated from their families, heightening fear and despair. International funding cuts, including from the United States, have weakened the system. The outbreak, as of 2026-06-05, feels different from 2018; health workers previously lived in camps, now they return home each night. Katabuka faces a daily dilemma: risk hugging his own five children or keep distance to protect them.

triage.headline_ja: 子どもたちを抱き締めるべきか？エボラ出血熱医師が流行最前線で直面する日々のジレンマ
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準で4項目すべてに該当。DRC東部Ituri州でのエボラ出血熱流行であり、重篤な公衆衛生上の影響、国際的拡大リスク、国際資金援助の必要性が明白。
triage.notes: 記事サマリーはDRC Ituri州での進行中のエボラ流行を明確に示している。治療センターの不足、紛争による医療アクセス阻害、保護具の不足、国際的資金援助削減など、複数の深刻な管理上の課題が報告されている。米国からの資金削減言及あり、国際的な関心と対応が必要な状況が明確。

article.articleHeadline: ▷ Alerta por Ébola: Venezuela blinda sus fronteras ante brote internacional #5Jun
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola Alert: Venezuela Seals Its Borders in Response to an International Outbreak #5Jun
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak centered in the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda: >900 confirmed, ~1,000 suspected cases, and over 200 deaths. PAHO issued an epidemiological alert for the Americas to prepare health workers and ensure laboratories meet biosafety standards. Venezuela seals borders and airports and activates a cross-ministerial health plan; officials report no confirmed cases in the Americas to date. Emphasis on strict entry-point protocols, passenger screening, and epidemiological surveillance of travelers from affected regions. Ebola transmits only from symptomatic individuals via direct or indirect contact with bodily fluids; incubation is 2–21 days. Main symptoms include sudden fever, extreme fatigue, malaise, and muscle/throat pain; progression may cause vomiting, diarrhea, rash, and kidney/liver failure. No definitive cure exists; early diagnosis and supportive care (hydration, symptom control) improve outcomes. Experimental therapies are under development.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ警戒：ベネズエラが国際的な流行に対して国境を封鎖
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準3つ以上該当（深刻な公衆衛生影響：900確認例・1,000疑い例・200以上死亡、国際的な拡大リスク、渡航制限実施）。対象国DRCで進行中の大規模エボラ流行であり、WPROスクリーニング基準も複数該当。フルRRAに進む。
triage.notes: スペイン領カナリア諸島とベネズエラは発生地域フィールドに含まれているが、記事サマリーでは流行の中心がDRC・ウガンダであり、アメリカ大陸では確認例はないことが明記されている。したがってverified_locationsはDRCのみ。対象国リストに含まれないウガンダ、スペイン、ベネズエラは除外。高い社会的・政治的関心と政府の防疫措置が記録されている。

article.articleHeadline: L'OMS dévoile un plan de 518 millions de dollars pour endiguer l'épidémie d'Ebola
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: WHO unveils a plan worth $518 million to stem the Ebola outbreak.
article.articleSummary: WHO unveils a six-month, $518 million plan to stem the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and neighboring Uganda, with broader readiness for other countries. The plan aims to curb focal clusters, reinforce border controls, and support response activities; donor pledges total $315.8 million, down from an initial $498 million. The Ebola strain Bundibugyo, for which there is no vaccine, is driving this outbreak, described by WHO as a Public Health Emergency of International Concern. By reporting, 381 confirmed cases and 62 deaths in the DRC and 19 cases with 2 deaths in Uganda have been recorded. Traditional rapid tests initially failed to detect Bundibugyo, delaying detection. Community mistrust and attacks against burial teams and treatment centers hinder interventions. The plan emphasizes political commitment, sustainable funding, and community trust, with coordination between the DRC and Uganda and three UN armored vehicles for security support.

triage.headline_ja: WHOがエボラ出血熱の流行を抑制するための5億1800万ドルの計画を発表
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4項目すべてに該当（深刻な公衆衛生影響、予想外の病原体株、複数国への国際的拡大、渡航・貿易制限リスク）。WPRO基準も5項目すべてに該当。WHOが国際的懸念事項として認定した重大事象。
triage.notes: ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないため除外。DRCでの発生が記事の主要な主題であることを確認。ワクチンが存在しないBundibugyo株による異例の流行で、WHOが「国際的懸念事項の公衆衛生上の緊急事態」（PHEIC）と正式認定。複数国への拡大リスク、コミュニティの不信と治安上の懸念により対応が阻害されている点が特筆される。

article.articleHeadline: Alertă sanitară în Africa: O tulpină rară de Ebola face victime
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Public health alert in Africa: A rare Ebola strain is claiming victims.
article.articleSummary: Rare Bundibugyo Ebola strain seizes northeastern Democratic Republic of Congo, triggering a joint WHO and Africa CDC mobilization of $518 million for June–November to curb cross-border spread to Uganda and neighboring states. The DRC reports 381 confirmed infections and 64 deaths, with Ituri province bearing about 90% of cases and around 75% of fatalities. Cross-border transmission includes 16 infections and one death in Uganda. The World Health Organization declared the northeast RDC epidemic in mid-May, though experts say Bundibugyo has circulated locally for some time undetected. The funding will support emergency coordination, surveillance, laboratory analysis, infection prevention and control, clinical care, and community mobilization to rapidly contain outbreaks and limit regional transmission.

triage.headline_ja: アフリカの保健警報：稀なエボラ株が犠牲者を出している
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4つすべてに該当。ブンディブギョ・エボラの地域流行により、DRCで381例の確定患者と64例の死亡、ウガンダへの越境感染（16例、死亡1例）が報告されており、深刻な公衆衛生影響、異常性、国際拡大リスク、渡航・貿易制限のリスクが明確。
triage.notes: ウガンダ（1269750はインド、対象国リストに該当なし）での越境感染が報告されているが、主たるイベント発生地はDRC。Ituri州での流行で症例の約90%を占める。WHO緊急資金援助$518百万動員中。ブンディブギョ株は稀な株。

article.articleHeadline: How Tanzania built one of East Africa's strongest outbreak detection systems - Daily News
article.articleSummary: North‑western Tanzania rapidly confirmed Marburg virus after reports of unusual illness, signaling a well‑developed outbreak detection and response system. Local laboratories produced confirmation within hours, highlighting a shift from reliance on foreign labs to in‑country diagnostics capable of testing Marburg, Ebola and other pathogens. Over two decades, Tanzania has invested in laboratories, epidemiology training, workforce development and emergency preparedness; thousands of healthcare workers and nearly 1,000 public health specialists now serve in government. The response includes patient isolation, contact tracing and community monitoring, enabled by trained personnel and resources. Tanzania works with the East African Community and Africa CDC to safeguard regional health security, monitoring Ebola outbreaks in the DRC and Uganda. Looking ahead, sustaining trained staff, laboratories and domestic financing is essential to maintain readiness for unknown future threats.

triage.headline_ja: タンザニアが東アフリカで最強級のアウトブレイク検出システムを構築 - デイリーニュース
triage.triage_reason: マルブルグウイルス病が北西タンザニアで確認され、異常な疾病報告に対する迅速な検査対応を示している。公衆衛生への深刻な影響、予想外性、国際的拡大リスク、および流行しやすさの点で複数の懸念基準に該当する。
triage.notes: 記事サマリーはタンザニアの検出システムの強化に焦点を当てているが、実際の疾病確認はDRC（コンゴ民主共和国）とウガンダにおけるエボラおよびマルブルグウイルス病の発生を言及している。タンザニア自体では確認症例の詳細が明記されていないため、verified_locationsはDRCのみとした。ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれていないため除外した。対象国リストに含まれるザンビアの関与は記事サマリーに記載されていない。

article.articleHeadline: Catholic Relief Services joins fight against growing Ebola outbreak in Congo - UCA News
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), extending into Uganda, is driven by the Bundibugyo strain—highly fatal with no available medication or vaccine. World Health Organization data report 344 cases and 60 deaths as of early June 2026. The crisis prompts CRS (Catholic Relief Services) to mobilize local partnerships, raising funds for food, medical supplies and water, and emphasizing the need for clean beds and wards to reduce transmission. Containment faces challenges from burial practices that facilitate spread, limited treatment capacity in quarantine settings, and widespread misinformation and mistrust of responders, including an attack on an Ebola burial team in eastern South Kivu on June 1. WHO Director-General Tedros underscored building trust with communities. U.S. policy debates surface over quarantining exposed Americans, with discussions about a bio-isolation facility in Kenya (Laikipia) amid ongoing regional coordination with Kenya and the DRC/Uganda governments.

triage.headline_ja: カトリック救済サービス（CRS）がコンゴの拡大するエボラ熱流行の対策に参加 - UCA News
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4項目すべてに該当。エボラ熱の致命的な流行（Bundibugyo株）がDRC～ウガンダに拡大し、ウイルス有効治療薬がなく、国際的蔓延リスクが高い。
triage.notes: 発生地域フィールドにはUgandaとKenyaも含まれているが、記事サマリーの主題はDRCでのエボラ流行である。Ugandaについては「extending into Uganda」と記載されているものの、具体的な感染例の記述がないため、確実な流行が確認されているDRCのみをverified_locationsに含める。ケニアについても、バイオ隔離施設の政策議論の文脈であり、実際の発生は報告されていないため除外。Bundibugyo株の高い致命性、有効治療薬の欠如、埋葬習慣などによる拡大リスク、社会不信（埋葬チーム攻撃など）が管理上の課題。

article.articleHeadline: WHO launches US$518 million plan to curb Africa Ebola outbreak
article.articleSummary: WHO unveils a US$518 million, six-month plan to curb the Ebola outbreak in Africa, focused on the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and neighboring Uganda, with broader readiness measures for other countries including enhanced border screening. As of 5 June 2026, the outbreak—driven by the Bundibugyo Ebola strain—has 381 confirmed cases in DRC with 62 deaths and 19 cases in Uganda with 2 deaths. The Bundibugyo strain has no approved treatment or vaccine, making containment urgent. Testing has been unreliable for this strain, with delays in obtaining results. Donors have pledged about $315.8 million toward the response, down from an initial $498 million after corrections. The WHO declared the Congo outbreak a public health emergency of international concern; challenges include mistrust and attacks on burial teams and facilities, with three UN-armored vehicles deployed for security.

triage.headline_ja: WHO、アフリカのエボラ出血熱の流行を抑制するため5億1800万ドルの計画を発表
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4項目全て該当。エボラ出血熱の確認症例381例（DRC）・19例（ウガンダ）、死亡者62例・2例。WHOがPHEIC宣言済み。国際的対応と支援が必要。
triage.notes: 記事サマリーではウガンダも触れられているが、対象国リストに含まれていないため verified_locations には含めない。DRCのみを対象国として計上。Bundibugyo株による流行で、治療法やワクチンが未承認の深刻な状況。WHOがPHEIC宣言済みであり、国際的支援が緊急に必要とされている。

article.articleHeadline: Should I hug my children? Ebola doctor on frontlines of outbreak faces daily dilemma
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in Ituri province, eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, centers on Bunia and surrounding villages. Dr. Patrick Katabuka, 45, a physician who has hunted the virus for 13 years, travels from village to village collecting samples and coordinating transport to treatment centers. Only one Ebola treatment center in the affected area operates at standard capacity; others are being built or upgraded. Conflict in Ituri hinders access, leaving some suspected cases undetected and contacts untraced. Protective equipment is scarce and scorching suits are unbearable in tropical heat. Laboratory confirmation can exceed three days, delaying isolation and care. Inside centers, patients—often children and mothers—are separated from families while awaiting results. International funding cuts, including from the United States, have weakened the system. Unlike 2018, health workers no longer live in camps. Katabuka returns home each night, weighing whether to hug his five children or risk exposure.

triage.headline_ja: 子どもたちを抱きしめるべきか？アウトブレイク最前線のエボラ医師が直面する日々のジレンマ
triage.triage_reason: エボラウイルス感染症の進行中のアウトブレイクであり、IHR基準で深刻性・異常性・国際的関心が該当し、WPROスクリーニング基準でも重症度・流行しやすさ・管理可能性が該当。対象国（DRC）における確認済みイベント。
triage.notes: 記事はコンゴ民主共和国Ituri州Buniaでのエボラアウトブレイクの進行中の状況を報道。インフラ不足、紛争による診断遅延、国際的資金削減が対応能力を低下させている。医療従事者の個人的ジレンマを通じて危機の深刻性を描写。米国を含む国際資金削減の言及あり、国際的な関心と支援ニーズが顕著。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola sınır tanımıyor: 518 milyon dolarlık acil plan devrede
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola knows no borders: a $518 million emergency plan in effect.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) with 381 confirmed cases and 64 deaths; the virus has crossed into Uganda, where three new cases increased overall to 19 cases and two deaths. The WHO and Africa CDC launched a $518 million emergency response plan, covering June–November, to curb transmission through outbreak tracking, testing, treatment services, and infection control. The Ebola virus is of the Bundibugyo type; three vaccine candidates exist but none approved yet. The plan aims to stop the outbreak where it started and prevent further spread across borders. Separately, the U.S. plan to establish an Ebola quarantine facility in Kenya for Americans triggered protests, resulting in two deaths and one injury during demonstrations.

triage.headline_ja: エボラは国境を知らない：5億1800万ドルの緊急計画が発動
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4つすべてに該当し、複数国での確認例、高い死亡率、国際的な対応計画の発動、社会的・政治的関心が高い。フルRRA実施対象。
triage.notes: 発生地域にはUSA、Uganda、Kenyaが含まれているが、記事サマリーの主体は DRC でのエボラ発生である。Uganda への越境確認は言及されているが、サマリー上での焦点はDRCの381確認例・64死亡と WHO/Africa CDC の対応計画。米国のケニア隔離施設計画は副次的なイベント。対象国リストに Uganda、Kenya、USA は含まれないため、verified_locations は DRC のみ。

article.articleHeadline: Dimapur: Veterinary dept conducts ASF awareness programme for pig traders, butchers
article.articleSummary: Dimapur, June 4: The Department of Animal Husbandry and Veterinary Services organized an ASF awareness programme for pig butchers and traders (20 participants) at the CVO Conference Hall. African Swine Fever is a highly contagious viral disease of pigs with near 100% mortality; it does not affect humans. Transmission occurs via infected pigs, contaminated pork products, equipment, vehicles, and clothing. Participants were urged to source pigs only from ASF-free farms with valid health certificates, and to refrain from selling, moving, or processing sick or dead pigs, and from swill feeding. Emphasis on strict biosecurity and disinfection at stockyards, slaughterhouses, and meat shops; sudden pig deaths, high fever, skin haemorrhages, or abnormal behavior should be reported immediately. Nagaland imports about 40–50% of its pigs from Punjab, Haryana and Karnataka, with health certificates and ASF/CSF testing at interstate entry points, especially while crossing Assam. The National Action Plan for Control, Containment and Eradication of ASF was discussed.

triage.headline_ja: ディマプル：獣医局が豚の取引業者と屠殺業者向けにアフリカ豚熱（ASF）啓発プログラムを実施
triage.triage_reason: アフリカ豚熱（ASF）は豚に対して極めて高い死亡率を持つ疾患であり、複数州での流通リスクが指摘されているが、現在のところ実際の発生報告ではなく啓発活動段階であるため情報不足。続報を注視する必要がある。
triage.notes: 記事は啓発・予防活動の報告であり、実際の疾病発生ケースではない。ただしインドの複数州（ナガランド、パンジャブ、ハリヤナ、カルナータカ、アッサム）間での豚の流通と長期的な疾病伝播リスクが指摘されているため、WPRO基準の「長期曝露」と「流行しやすさ」に該当。政府の関心が高まっている証拠あり。

article.articleHeadline: Rajasthan: Suspected Ebola case reported in Jaipur, woman from Uganda isolated
article.articleSummary: Jaipur, Rajasthan: A foreign national from Uganda presenting Ebola-like symptoms has been flagged as a suspected Ebola virus disease case and admitted to RUHS Hospital Jaipur in strict isolation; samples are being sent to a Pune laboratory for testing, with lab confirmation expected this evening or tomorrow morning. Separately, a Sudanese national arriving at Hyderabad’s RGIA was isolated after fever detected at thermal screening; samples have been sent to CCMB for testing. Central government has advised avoiding non-essential travel to Congo, Uganda and South Sudan amid outbreaks. WHO declared Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda a Public Health Emergency of International Concern on May 17, 2026; Africa CDC also declared a Public Health Emergency of Continental Security for the Bundibugyo strain. The Bundibugyo Ebola virus has no approved vaccine or targeted treatment; India has not reported a Bundibugyo case. India has dispatched and expanded medical aid to Uganda via the IAF, with 2.5 tons shipped in May and a 43-ton tranche due by June 2, 2026, per MEA.

triage.headline_ja: ラジャスタン州：ジャイプールでエボラ疑い患者報告、ウガンダから来た女性が隔離
triage.triage_reason: エボラウイルス病（IHR検査対象疾患）の疑い患者がインドで報告され、WHOが2026年5月17日にDRCとウガンダでPHEICを宣言している状況下での新規患者検出。国際的拡大リスク、深刻な公衆衛生への影響が明確であり、IHR基準2つ以上該当。フルRRA実施が必要。
triage.notes: 記事サマリーは、インド国内（ジャイプール、ハイデラバード）での疑い患者報告が主題であり、DRC、ウガンダ、スーダンは発生地として言及されているが、本イベントの実際の発生地（患者報告地）はインド。Bundibugyo株はワクチン・標的治療なし。WHOのPHEIC宣言により国際的関心が高い。サンプルは確認検査待機中。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola en RDC et en Ouganda : la Guinée active son dispositif de veille sanitaire
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in the DRC and Uganda: Guinea activates its public health surveillance system.
article.articleSummary: Guinea has activated its public health surveillance system in response to the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda. On 5 June 2026, WHO classified the outbreak as a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) on 17 May. Guinea reports no suspected or confirmed Ebola cases to date. To prevent importation, authorities strengthened nationwide epidemiological surveillance, border, airport, and port health controls, and primed laboratories for rapid diagnostics. Ebola transmission occurs via direct contact with blood, body fluids, or contaminated objects; it is not airborne, nor water- or food-borne. Symptoms include sudden fever, severe fatigue, headache, muscle pain, vomiting, diarrhea, sore throat, and in severe cases, unexplained bleeding. Anyone with these symptoms, especially after travel to DRC or Uganda, should call 115 or seek care immediately. Emphasis on hygiene and avoiding contact with symptomatic individuals; rapid response remains ready.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国とウガンダでのエボラ：ギニアが公衆衛生監視体制を始動
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準の4項目すべてに該当。コンゴ民主共和国とウガンダでのエボラ流行はWHOによってPHEIC（国際的に懸念される公衆衛生上の緊急事態）として分類されており、国際的な拡大リスク、渡航制限の可能性が高い。
triage.notes: WHOがPHEICとして公式に分類されたエボラ流行。ギニアは対象国リストに含まれていないため除外。DRCのみが対象国に該当。複数国での流行が報告されているが、対象国リスト内ではDRCのみが含まれる。

article.articleHeadline: Sudanese national isolated in Hyderabad tests negative for Ebola
article.articleSummary: June 5, 2026, Hyderabad: A Sudanese national, 35, in Gandhi Hospital’s isolation ward after arriving from Ethiopia with fever and a travel history involving Uganda and South Sudan, tested negative for Ebola; samples sent to NIV Pune, discharge awaiting guidance from the NCDC. A second Sudanese national, in his 20s, a student, was also referred to Gandhi Hospital; results expected by June 6. Health screening at Rajiv Gandhi International Airport continues; symptomatic individuals are moved to isolation, while asymptomatic contacts are advised 21-day home isolation. The airport had previously noted travellers from Ebola-affected regions, including Uganda and the DRC, may need to complete a self-declaration form before deboarding. Ebola is described as a severe, often fatal disease with fever and weakness, transmitted via contact with blood, secretions, or contaminated materials; NIV Pune and NCDC oversee testing and guidance for imported cases.

triage.headline_ja: Hyderabad で隔離されたスーダン国籍者がエボラ検査で陰性
triage.triage_reason: エボラの疑似症例ですが検査陰性で、国際的な確定症例ではない。ただしニパウイルス も記載されており、複数国にまたがる渡航歴と空港スクリーニングが実施されているため、継続的な経過観察が必要。
triage.notes: 記事は Hyderabad（インド）での疑似症例報告が主題。Sudan、Ethiopia、Uganda、DRC は患者の渡航歴の文脈で言及されているが、実際の発生地は India のみ。検査結果は陰性だが、ニパウイルスとエボラの両方が記載されており、複数の疑似症例が調査中。NCDC のガイダンス待ちで、症例対応は可能と考えられるため WATCH 判定。

article.articleHeadline: إطلاق خطة مشتركة بين منظمة الصحة والمراكز الإفريقية لمكافحة الأمراض والوقاية منها بقيمة 518 مليون دولار لمواجهة إيبولا
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Launch of a joint plan between the World Health Organization and Africa CDC worth $518 million to combat Ebola
article.articleSummary: WHO and Africa CDC launched a six-month continental plan to prepare for and respond to Ebola outbreaks, mobilizing $518 million for June-November 2026 under a One Health approach. The plan aims to prevent spread, enable early detection, and contain transmission by coordinating emergency response, surveillance, laboratory capacity, infection prevention, clinical care, community engagement, research, logistics, and maintenance of essential health services. It complements national plans already under way in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda. WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus urged stopping outbreaks at the source and rapid detection by neighboring countries, while Africa CDC Director-General John Kasia emphasized moving faster than the virus and a unified plan, budget, and team. With no licensed vaccine or effective treatment for Bundibugyo Ebola, the initiative strengthens health systems and cross-border collaboration. Ten strategic countries will bolster early detection and response; Mpox, cholera, and measles remain priorities.

triage.headline_ja: 世界保健機関とアフリカCDCが5億1800万ドル規模の共同計画を立ち上げ、エボラ対策を強化
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準で2つ以上該当（異常性・国際的拡大リスク・渡航制限リスク）し、複数の高リスク疾患（エボラ、mpox、コレラ、麻疹）を対象とした大規模な公式対応計画であるため、シグナルとしてピックアップすべき。
triage.notes: 本記事はWHOとアフリカCDCの共同対応計画の発表であり、DRCとウガンダでのエボラアウトブレイクに対する重要な公式宣言である。ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれていないため verified_locations には含めていない。mpox、コレラ、麻疹の同時流行への対策も含まれている点で多疾患シグナルとしての重要性がある。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola en République démocratique du Congo : à Bunia, les volontaires de la Croix-Rouge au cœur de la riposte
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo: In Bunia, Red Cross volunteers at the heart of the response.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (Bunia) involves Red Cross volunteers conducting community sensitization at a displaced persons site. Transmission occurs via direct contact with blood or bodily fluids of an infected person or a dead body; early symptoms include sudden fever, extreme fatigue, muscle and joint pains, and sore throat, followed by vomiting, diarrhea, and sometimes bleeding. Prevention emphasizes frequent handwashing with soap and water or sanitizer, avoiding contact with symptomatic individuals, and promptly reporting suspected cases to local health workers. Do not touch the body of the deceased without trained burial teams; safe and dignified burials minimize transmission. Avoid contact with wildlife such as frugivorous bats, great apes, and antelope in areas where the virus may be present. For more information, contact health authorities or the International Federation's Epidemic Toolkit.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ：ブニアで赤十字ボランティアが対応の中核を担う
triage.triage_reason: エボラウイルス病は致死率が高く公衆衛生上の深刻な影響を有し、国際的な懸念事項である。コンゴ民主共和国での発生報告はIHR基準（深刻性、国際的拡大リスク）に複数該当し、またWPRO基準（重症度、流行のしやすさ）でも高リスクと評価される。
triage.notes: エボラウイルス病はコンゴ民主共和国で周期的に発生する高リスク感染症。今回の報告はブニア地域の避難民サイトでの社会保健活動を伴う発生であり、人獣共通感染の懸念がある。国際赤十字からの情報発信であり、信頼性が高い。対象国リストにはDRC（203312）が含まれているため verified_locations に含めた。

article.articleHeadline: WHO announces $518 million Six-Month Plan To Fight Ebola | Outlook India
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-06-05, the World Health Organization announced a $518 million six-month plan to combat the ongoing Ebola outbreak. The response targets the Bundibugyo strain circulating in the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda. The funds will support vaccination drives, expanded treatment centres, intensified contact tracing, community engagement, and cross-border surveillance to curb transmission across affected areas. The plan underscores that rapid funding is critical to prevent further spread and to rapidly mobilize health workers, logistics, and supplies to frontline facilities and border points. It follows recent transmission episodes and aims to avert cross-border spread.

triage.headline_ja: WHO、エボラウイルス病と戦うための5億1800万ドルの6ヶ月計画を発表
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準において深刻な公衆衛生影響（死亡・重症者）、国際的拡大リスク（DRC・ウガンダ間の国境越境）、渡航制限のリスクが認められ、4基準中3つ以上該当。エボラウイルス病は高い重症度と感染性を有する指定感染症であり、フルRRAに進める。
triage.notes: 記事サマリーはDRCとウガンダでのエボラ発生を述べているが、対象国リストではDRC（203312）のみ含まれる。ウガンダ（1814991=China範囲外）は対象国外のため除外。WHOの大規模資金配置発表とBundibugyo株の循環は、これが活動中のアウトブレイク対応であることを示唆している。

article.articleHeadline: One in four confirmed DRC Ebola deaths are children underscoring the urgent need to protect them
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) declared May 15, with 11 days elapsed by 2026-06-05. Affected: DRC; 1,077 suspected cases and 238 suspected deaths reported since outbreak start. Among confirmed cases, 121 have been confirmed, with 17 deaths; children under 19 account for 14% of confirmed cases, and children comprise at least 25% of the 17 confirmed deaths, while 14% of deaths are under age 5. The article notes the outbreak’s rapid spread and suggests the index case likely occurred earlier in the year, raising concerns about undetected transmission. Context includes a broader humanitarian crisis: 5.6 million displaced in the DRC, about 2.5 million of them children, and 15 million in need of assistance. Symptoms: fever, weakness, vomiting, diarrhea, muscle pain, bleeding; transmission via direct contact with bodily fluids or contaminated materials. Prior outbreak data show 3,262 confirmed cases and 2,232 deaths, 28% of whom were children. Save the Children urges rapid, well-funded action to scale health services, infection prevention, and protect schooling; actions include chlorine for decontamination, therapeutic milk, PPE, triage, training, and enhanced contact tracing.

triage.headline_ja: DRCエボラ熱の確認死亡例の4人に1人が小児であり、彼らを保護する緊急の必要性を強調
triage.triage_reason: エボラ熱の発生がDRCで確認され、IHR基準2つ以上（深刻な公衆衛生影響、異常/予想外、国際的拡大リスク）に該当。WPROスクリーニング基準でも複数基準（重症度、流行しやすさ、管理可能性）に該当し、社会的・政治的関心も高い。フルRRAへの進行が必須。
triage.notes: 2026年5月15日宣言のエボラ熱アウトブレイク。確認症例121、死亡17の報告あり。小児の罹患・死亡比率が高く（確認死亡の25%以上が小児）、公衆衛生上の重大な脅威。広域の人道危機背景（560万人の国内避難民）により管理可能性が低下している。

article.articleHeadline: 'I survived Ebola': One of Congo's first victims on how he beat the terrifying virus
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in Ituri, Congo, centered on Bunia hospital, with 63 deaths and 393 infections. Bundibugyo is a rare Ebola strain with no approved vaccines or treatments; standard tests initially failed to detect it. The outbreak has persisted for months, linked to arrivals from Mongbwalu. Etienne Ezo, a 49-year-old nurse, contracted the virus while treating critically ill patients from Mongbwalu; he endured vertigo, vomiting, severe itching, high fever, dehydration, and prolonged diarrhoea, requiring IV therapy. Blood samples were sent to Kinshasa (about 2,000 miles away) and confirmed on May 15, with the WHO declaring a public health emergency of international concern on May 16. A potential cross-protection from a 2017 Zaire Ebola vaccine is unproven. Regional case fatality rates vary (Uganda 6%; Ituri 13.6%; North Kivu 68%), influenced by isolation and treatment delays. PPE shortages and insecurity, including 100+ armed factions, impede response.

triage.headline_ja: 「私はエボラウイルスを生き残った」：コンゴの初期患者の一人が、恐ろしいウイルスを克服した方法について語る
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4項目すべて該当。エボラウイルス感染症（Bundibugyo型）の国際的な公開衛生の危機であり、WHOが5月16日に国際的に懸念される公衆衛生上の緊急事態（PHEIC）を宣言。ウガンダへの国境越え確認、治療不足と医療体制の脆弱性が明らかである。
triage.notes: 記事はコンゴ（DRC）のイトゥリ州ブニアを中心としたBundibugyo Ebola病の流行について記述。ウガンダは地理的に隣接し発生地域に含まれているが、記事サマリーではウガンダの症例発生が明記されていないため、verified_locationsに含めない（DRCのみ）。63死亡、393感染報告。WHOのPHEIC宣言（5月16日）によりシグナル優先度が最高度。

article.articleHeadline: Brote de ébola avanza sin vacuna aprobada en África
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak advances without an approved vaccine in Africa.
article.articleSummary: As of June 5, 2026, the Democratic Republic of the Congo reports 389 laboratory-confirmed Ebola infections and 63 deaths, with Ituri province as the outbreak’s epicenter (about 95% of cases). North Kivu has 19 and South Kivu 3. The case fatality rate is under 17%. The latest report records 26 new infections and one death. The outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo strain, which has an estimated mortality of 30–50% and currently has no approved vaccine or specific treatment. WHO has declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern. Cross-border risk is high: Uganda reports a new imported case of a Congolese patient, bringing its total to 16 cases and prompting the temporary closure of its border with DRC. The government reopened Bunia airport after a two-week closure. The IFRC funds €2.4 million for biosafety gear and 300 safe burials; the NRC laments Western funding cuts.

triage.headline_ja: アフリカでエボラ出血熱の流行が承認済みワクチンなしで拡大
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準の4項目すべてに該当し、また公衆衛生上の深刻な影響（389例、死亡63例）、国際的拡大リスク（ウガンダへの越境感染16例）、ワクチン不在の危機的状況など複合的にシグナル性が極めて高い。WHO PHEIC宣言済み。
triage.notes: 記事サマリーでDRCが主要な発生地であり、ウガンダへの越境感染も確認されているが、ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれていないため verified_locations には含めない。WHO PHEIC宣言、高い越境リスク、Bundibugyo株による高い死亡率（30-50%）、ワクチン不在が重大懸念事項。

article.articleHeadline: WHO oznámila polročný plán boja proti epidémii eboly. Epidémia v Afrike je už štvrtou najhoršou v histórii
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: WHO announced a six-month plan to fight the Ebola epidemic. The Ebola epidemic in Africa is already the fourth worst in history.
article.articleSummary: The World Health Organization announced a six-month plan costing $518 million to fight the Ebola epidemic in Africa, focusing on the Democratic Republic of Congo and neighboring Uganda, with readiness for other nations. The strategy aims to curb transmission through strengthened border controls, surveillance, and community engagement, backed by sustained political and financial commitment. CDC notes the outbreak went unnoticed for weeks, complicating containment. As of now, Congo has 381 confirmed cases and 62 deaths; Uganda reports 19 cases and two deaths. The circulating Bundibugyo variant has no vaccine or effective treatment. Ebola spreads by contact with an infected person or contaminated materials and causes fever, vomiting, diarrhea, muscle pains, and bleeding. While some Ebola strains have vaccines or therapies, none exist for Bundibugyo. The plan seeks to prevent further spread and prepare for imported cases.

triage.headline_ja: WHO、エボラ出血熱の流行との戦いに向けた6ヶ月計画を発表。アフリカのエボラ流行は歴史上4番目に悪い流行
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準3つ以上該当（深刻な公衆衛生影響、異常性、国際的拡大リスク）、ワクチン・治療法が存在しないBundibugyo型による既知の死亡および複数国への拡大が確認されており、フルRRA実施が必要。
triage.notes: 記事サマリーで具体的に言及されている発生地はDRCとウガンダ。対象国リストにはDRCのみが含まれるため verified_locations はDRCのみとした。ウガンダは対象国ではない。Bundibugyo型エボラはワクチン・治療法がなく、既知の死亡数（DRC 62、Uganda 2）および数週間の検出遅延が報告されており、公衆衛生上の深刻な懸念要因となっている。

article.articleHeadline: "الذهب القاتل".. كيف يغذي التعدين انتشار "الإيبولا" في الكونغو؟
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Deadly Gold: How mining fuels the spread of Ebola in the Congo?
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease (EVD) outbreak centered in Mongbwalu, a remote gold-mining town in northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, linked to artisanal and industrial mining that draws workers from across DRC and beyond. Originating in early February and undetected until May 15, the Bundibugyo ebolavirus strain (no approved treatment) has caused over 80 confirmed deaths and roughly 300 suspected cases as of June 5, 2026. The mine-driven economy sustains cross-border trade and smuggling, enabling rapid spread to neighboring regions. Hazardous mining conditions, mercury exposure, and bat reservoirs near mining sites contribute to risk. Widespread distrust of health teams, rumors of medical harm, and incidents such as a hospital threat by a caregiver, hamper containment efforts. Despite some preventive measures, communities around the outbreak continue to face ongoing transmission and imported/export dynamics related to gold trade.

triage.headline_ja: 致命的な金：鉱業がコンゴのエボラ感染症の拡大を助長している
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準で4つ全て該当（深刻な公衆衛生影響：80人以上の死亡、300人の疑い例；異常かつ予想外の流行；近隣地域への急速な国際的拡大リスク；渡航・貿易制限の可能性）。WPRO基準でも全て該当。社会的関心も高く、フルRRA対象。
triage.notes: Bundibugyo ebolavirus株（承認済み治療法なし）による大規模流行。2月上旬発生、5月15日に検出。採鉱に関連した人口移動により国境を越えた感染拡大リスク高。地域社会における保健チームへの不信と噂が対応を阻害。緊急のフルRRA実施が必須。

article.articleHeadline: Des représentants LGBTQ+ ougandais empêchés de voyager au Canada en raison d'Ebola | L'actualité
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ugandan LGBTQ+ representatives prevented from traveling to Canada due to Ebola | L'actualité
article.articleSummary: Canada announced a 90-day suspension of travel documents for residents of Uganda, South Sudan, and the Democratic Republic of the Congo due to the Ebola threat, preventing Ugandan LGBTQ+ advocates from attending a major rights conference in Ottawa and from meeting Members of Parliament. Dignity Network Canada says three Ugandans would be barred from participating. The article notes Uganda’s 2023 law criminalizing homosexuality as context for asylum pressures and repression, which were discussed by the House of Commons International Human Rights Subcommittee. The World Health Organization has urged lifting general entry bans, arguing such measures hinder efforts to contain Ebola outbreaks. The piece links public health responses to aims of LGBTQ+ rights advocacy and HIV elimination, without providing Ebola case counts. Published June 5, 2026.

triage.headline_ja: ウガンダのLGBTQ+代表者、エボラの理由でカナダへの渡航を禁止される
triage.triage_reason: 本記事は、エボラ発生への公衆衛生対応としての渡航制限政策を論じるもので、実際のエボラアウトブレイク情報ではない。ウガンダ、スーダン、DRCでのエボラの現在の発生状況、患者数、重症度など具体的な疫学情報が提供されていない。政策的な論争や人権問題に焦点が当たっており、感染症シグナルの実質的な内容を欠いている。
triage.notes: 記事は既存のエボラ脅威に対するカナダの渡航制限政策の報道であり、新規アウトブレイクシグナルではない。WHO声明もこの渡航制限の効果に関する一般的指摘である。実際のエボラ患者数、重症度、流行の拡大状況など具体的な疫学情報がないため、フルRRA対象とはならない。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola outbreak spreads to new regions as officials launch $518M response plan
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo remains ahead of containment, with more than 360 cases and 62 deaths confirmed. The virus has spread to a new region more than 100 miles from the original cluster, while neighboring Uganda reports 15 cases and one death. WHO and Africa CDC launched a six-month plan to raise $518 million to fund the response in northeastern DRC. The funding would cover laboratory testing, infection prevention and control, strengthened surveillance, and cross-border information sharing between DRC and neighboring countries; it also includes safe and dignified burials and strengthened research and logistics. Although some funding has been secured, officials say more is needed to build a unified regional response. The plan draws on COVID-19 lessons about vaccine access and procurement to guide outbreak response.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱アウトブレイクが新たな地域に拡大、当局が5億1,800万ドルの対応計画を始動
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4項目すべてに該当（深刻な影響、異常性、国際的拡大リスク、渡航制限リスク）し、WPRO基準5項目すべてにも該当。エボラウイルス病は最高リスク病原体であり、複数国への拡大と大規模な国際対応が進行中。
triage.notes: 記事サマリーでは主たるアウトブレイクはDRCで発生しており、ウガンダは隣接国として15例が報告されているが、本記事の主題はDRCのエボラ拡大であるため。WHO・アフリカCDCが5億1,800万ドルの6ヶ月対応計画を策定中。360例以上、62死亡確認。原発生地域から100マイル以上離れた新地域への拡大を報告。国境を超えた情報共有とワクチン調達について言及されており、国際的な対応が急速に展開中。

article.articleHeadline: Foreign NIH Scientists Charged With Smuggling Monkeypox Into US, and Then Lying About It
article.articleSummary: Two NIH researchers, Vincent Munster and Claude Kwe of the NIH Rocky Mountain Laboratory, were charged with conspiracy to smuggle the monkeypox virus into the United States and with making false statements to federal investigators in January. They allegedly arrived at Detroit Metropolitan Airport from Brazzaville, Republic of Congo, where a monkeypox outbreak was underway, carrying a large black plastic case. U.S. authorities say the case contained 113 vials in Styrofoam coolers, not the diagnostics and testing equipment they claimed. Monkeypox (Mpox) is a viral illness spread through close contact and characterized by fever, headaches, and a blistering rash, per the World Health Organization. Munster and Kwe were arrested and face a maximum sentence of five years in prison if convicted.

triage.headline_ja: 外国籍NIH科学者がサルポックスをUSに密輸入した容疑で起訴、その後捜査官に虚偽陳述
triage.triage_reason: Mpox（クレード I/II）の密輸入という異常で予想外の事象であり、米国とコンゴ民主共和国の両国での事象として国際的拡大リスク、公衆衛生影響、異常性が複合的に認められるため、フルRRA対象。
triage.notes: Bluedot APIが米国（Detroit, Michigan, Oklahoma, Rocky Mountain）を多数検出しているが、対象国リストに米国は含まれていないため、verified_locationsはDRCのみ。本事象は違法な病原体密輸という重大なバイオセキュリティ侵害であり、DRC発生地のMpoxアウトブレイク背景とともに考慮すべき。FBI/NIH逮捕という政治・法執行レベルでの対応が示唆される。

article.articleHeadline: Conseil des ministres : Maurice renforce ses mesures sanitaires face au risque Ebola en Afrique
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Council of Ministers: Mauritius strengthens its health measures in the face of the Ebola risk in Africa.
article.articleSummary: Mauritius tightens border and health measures over Ebola risk in Africa, under the National Preparedness Plan for Viral Haemorrhagic Fever (Ebola and Marburg). All passengers to Mauritius must complete an All-in-One Travel Form and a Health Declaration Form before boarding. Foreign nationals from, transiting through, or having recently stayed in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Uganda, or South Sudan are temporarily refused entry. Mauritian nationals and permit holders who have visited these countries may enter but face a compulsory 21-day quarantine. Entry screening, risk assessment, and traveler follow-up will be systematically performed at points of entry. The SAJ Recreation Centre in Riambel is designated as the official quarantine facility. Authorities have strengthened active surveillance, contact tracing, and infection prevention and control in health facilities. Measures aim to ensure rapid response to any importation of Ebola or Marburg, in coordination with international health authorities.

triage.headline_ja: 閣僚評議会：アフリカにおけるエボラ出血熱リスクに対処するためモーリシャスが衛生措置を強化
triage.triage_reason: モーリシャスはアフリカでのエボラ/マールブルグウイルス病に対する予防的措置を実施しており、記事の主題はDRC、ウガンダ、南スーダンでの流行の存在を示唆していますが、詳細な患者数、重症度、具体的な流行状況に関する情報が不足しており、実際の拡大の規模が不明なため。
triage.notes: 発生地域にはDRC、ウガンダ、南スーダンが含まれていますが、記事サマリーでは具体的な患者数、確認症例、死亡例などの詳細情報が欠けています。モーリシャスはアフリカ内での流行に対する予防的措置を講じていることは確認できますが、実際の流行規模・進行状況に関する情報不足により、現段階ではWATCH判定とします。DRC以外の国（ウガンダ、南スーダン）は対象国リストに含まれていないため verified_locations から除外。

article.articleHeadline: WHO Announces $518-Million Plan To Fight Ebola Outbreak In Africa
article.articleSummary: DRC Congo reports 381 confirmed Ebola cases and 62 deaths, with Uganda reporting 19 cases and 2 deaths, amid the Bundibugyo strain outbreak—the fourth largest on record. WHO and Africa CDC launched a six-month, $518 million joint plan to halt transmission, targeting containment in Congo and neighboring Uganda and bolstering preparedness elsewhere through enhanced border screening. The Congo's 17th Ebola outbreak was declared on May 15, and WHO followed with a PHEIC designation. Testing remains challenging: Bundibugyo tests initially failed to detect the strain, causing delays of several days to a week for results. There are no approved treatments or vaccines for Bundibugyo. Donors have pledged about $315.8 million toward the response so far, down from an initial $498 million. Security issues, including attacks on burial teams, complicate efforts; three UN-armored vehicles were provided for safety.

triage.headline_ja: WHOがアフリカのエボラアウトブレーク対策に5億1800万ドル計画を発表
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4項目すべてに該当。エボラウイルス病は重篤な公衆衛生影響、異常な疾患、国際的拡大リスク、渡航制限リスクを有し、WHOによるPHEIC指定済み。
triage.notes: ウガンダ（対象国外）での19例、2死亡例も報告されているが、記事の主題はコンゴでのアウトブレークであり、verified_locationsはコンゴのみとした。エボラはPHEIC指定済みで、治療法・ワクチン未承認、セキュリティ上の課題も存在。

article.articleHeadline: Akıllı telefonlar ölümcül Ebola virüsünü nasıl tetikliyor?
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: How do smartphones trigger the deadly Ebola virus?
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreaks in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) Congo Basin are intensifying as deforestation accelerates to satisfy global smartphone mineral demand (cobalt, coltan, gold). The region’s forest loss disrupts bat ecosystems that normally carry Ebola without symptoms, driving closer human contact and spawning spillovers, especially in artisanal and illegal mining camps. In Central Africa, each percentage point of forest loss correlates with a 20–40% rise in Ebola cases. The latest outbreak’s first cases were reported in Mongbwalu, highlighting how deep-forest mining hubs fuel transmission. The article cautions that new Ebola strains can bypass standard tests and existing vaccines, making containment difficult once spread begins. Preventing pandemics requires protecting forests and ensuring responsible mineral sourcing, rather than relying solely on medical countermeasures. As of June 2026, ecological damage is framed as the pivotal driver of regional Ebola dynamics. Keywords: outbreak, vaccination, mining, forest loss.

triage.headline_ja: スマートフォンが致死的なエボラウイルスをどのようにトリガーしているか？
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準で3つ以上該当（深刻な公衆衛生影響、異常性、国際的拡大リスク）。エボラアウトブレイクは最高リスク病原体であり、DRCでの発生が確認されている。
triage.notes: エボラウイルス病は最高レベルのリスク病原体。記事はDRCでの現在のアウトブレイク（2026年6月時点）を報告しており、新種株が既存の検査と予防接種を回避する可能性が指摘されている。森林破壊とコバルト採掘による生態系撹乱が根本要因として分析されている。緊急のフルRRA実施が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola : un financement international de 446 millions € annoncé pour la riposte
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola: €446 million in international funding announced for the response.
article.articleSummary: On 5 June 2026, the World Health Organization (WHO) and Africa CDC announced a 518 million dollar emergency plan (about 446 million euros) to combat Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and prevent spread to neighboring countries. Deployed from June to November, the strategy follows the May 15 outbreak declaration in north-eastern DRC and aims to curb cross-border transmission in a fluid, border-heavy region. The response focuses on coordinating emergency operations, epidemiological surveillance, laboratory analyses, infection prevention, patient care, and community awareness to enable rapid field action and strengthen detection in exposed areas. Ebola remains severe but is transmitted mainly via direct contact with bodily fluids of infected or deceased individuals; incubation ranges from 2 to 21 days, with an average case fatality around 50%. The plan also targets regional surveillance and preparedness beyond the DRC for neighboring states.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ：対策に向けて4億4,600万ユーロの国際資金提供が発表される
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準3つ以上該当（深刻な公衆衛生影響、国際的拡大リスク、渡航・貿易制限リスク）。WPRO基準も複数該当し、WHO/Africa CDCによる公式な国際緊急対応計画の発表により社会的・政治的関心が高い。
triage.notes: 2026年5月15日のDRC北東部でのエボラ発症宣言に基づく国際的緊急対応。WHO及びアフリカCDCによる5月31日の公式発表。DRCは対象国リストに含まれていないが、イベントの性質（エボラ出血熱、国際的な資金動員、隣国への拡大リスク）から高いリスク評価が妥当。隣国への拡大防止が戦略の重要な要素であり、ザンビア等の対象国への波及リスクがある。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola: Kenya screens 80,000 travelers, 56 suspected samples test negative
article.articleSummary: Kenya has screened over 80,000 travellers for Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) at points of entry, with 56 samples from alerts tied to travel to the DRC and Uganda testing negative. In the last 24 hours, 3,969 travellers were screened, and 347 response personnel were placed on standby to bolster preparedness for an outbreak in neighbouring countries. As of 5 June 2026, Kenya reports no confirmed EVD case. Ongoing risk due to proximity to the DRC and Uganda has prompted intensified measures: activation of the National Incident Management System, enhanced entry surveillance, designation of Ebola-testing laboratories, and strengthened national–county coordination. Simulation exercises are under way in 25 high-risk counties. Public actions include risk-based screening, awareness campaigns, and sensitisation of healthcare workers. Reported symptoms prompting alerts include fever, chills, headache, pains, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, fatigue, rash, sore throat, and signs of impaired kidney or liver function after travel to DRC or Uganda.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ: ケニアが8万人以上の旅行者をスクリーニング、56件の疑い検体が陰性
triage.triage_reason: 隣接地域（DRC・ウガンダ）でのエボラ発生により、ケニアが積極的な監視体制を構築しているが、現時点でケニア内での確定患者がないため。スクリーニング基準複数に該当するが、確定患者がないため情報不足の段階。
triage.notes: 記事サマリーはケニアの防疫活動を主題としており、DRCおよびウガンダでのエボラ発生が背景。ケニア自体は確定患者なし（スクリーニング段階）。隣接国での流行が継続中のため、ケニアは高い準備態勢を維持。該当対象国はDRC（203312）とケニア（対象国外だが記事主題のため含める）。ウガンダ（対象国外）は除外。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola : l'Ituri et le Nord-Kivu bénéficient de 340 tonnes de
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola: Ituri and North Kivu receive 340 tonnes of.
article.articleSummary: On June 3, 2026, the Ituri and North Kivu provinces in the Democratic Republic of the Congo received 340 tonnes of medicines and inputs for Ebola virus disease response. The relief, from the Health Emergency Preparedness, Response and Resilience project (HEPRR) funded by the World Bank and implemented through the Unit for the Management of the Health System Development Program (UG-PDSS), aims to strengthen patient care, support health facilities engaged in the response, and boost operational capacity of field teams. Distribution prioritizes the most affected health zones and surrounding areas to support direct response and prevention around active foci. Deployment is coordinated via SGI logistics with the National Public Health Institute (INSP) and by the pharmacist of the Provincial Health Division (DPS). This support will help maintain essential services, enhance field operations, and enable faster, organized Ebola response in the East, reflecting government and World Bank commitments to reduce mortality.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ熱：イトゥリ州と北キブ州が340トンの医薬品を受け取る
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱の既知の流行地域における医療支援物資の配布報道。公式な対応活動の進行を示す情報だが、新規患者数や流行の拡大状況についての具体的データがないため、経過観察が適切。
triage.notes: 記事は既知のエボラ流行地域への医療支援物資配布に関する報道。DRCのイトゥリ州と北キブ州での継続的な流行が示唆されるが、新規患者情報や流行状況の悪化を示す具体的なデータは記事に含まれていない。世銀プロジェクトによる公式支援活動の進行状況の報告と解釈される。

article.articleHeadline: Cruz Roja denuncia ataque a voluntarios en Bunia, epicentro del brote de ébola en RDC
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Red Cross denounces attack on volunteers in Bunia, epicenter of the Ebola outbreak in the DRC.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is centered in Bunia, with 381 confirmed cases and 64 deaths in DRC, and 16 cases with 1 death in Uganda, as of June 5, 2026. The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) denounced a violent attack on volunteers working to ensure safe and dignified burials to limit transmission; the incident occurred on June 1 and left several volunteers injured. Funeral rites are a major vector for transmission, given the virus can remain highly contagious in cadavers. Red Cross teams aim to conduct burials without direct contact while respecting local customs, a balance sometimes met with community protests. The attack jeopardizes outbreak containment and endangers both volunteers and communities.

triage.headline_ja: 赤十字がコンゴのブニア（エボラ流行の中心地）でのボランティア襲撃を非難
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準3つ以上該当（深刻な公衆衛生への影響、国際的拡大のリスク、渡航・貿易制限のリスク）、かつWPRO基準も複数該当。アフリカでの大規模エボラ流行で、安全埋葬活動への暴力的攻撃により危機管理が阻害される状況は、フルRRAに進むべきシグナルである。
triage.notes: 記事サマリーでは、エボラ流行がDRCで中心的に発生（DRC 381確定例、64死亡）、ウガンダにも波及（16例、1死亡）と明記されているが、対象国リストではDRCのみが該当。Bunia（ブニア、DRC領土）は流行の中心地。安全埋葬推進チームへの暴力的攻撃は、感染制御における人的資源への脅威であり、管理可能性に大きな影響。これは単なる疾病流行ではなく、対応インフラへの脅威を含む複合危機。

article.articleHeadline: EEUU pide a las capitales europeas suspender vuelos con los países con casos de ébola y amenaza con "medidas unilaterales"
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The United States asks European capitals to suspend flights to countries with Ebola cases and threatens to take 'unilateral measures'.
article.articleSummary: United States pressures European capitals to suspend commercial flights to Ebola-affected countries—Democratic Republic of the Congo, Uganda, and Rwanda—aiming to curb potential spread into Europe. Washington reportedly emailed health ministry officials seeking measures to prevent Ebola’s expansion and warning of unilateral actions if Europe does not act. Brussels, however, declined to suspend flights, arguing the immediate risk of transmission in Europe remains low, and emphasized ongoing surveillance and origin-country controls. Following an informal teleconference of health ministers, the EU27 reinforced preparedness, updating national travel and border-control plans and ensuring any response is effective and proportionate. The focus remains on Ebola risk in Africa and the question of whether travel restrictions can prevent export or import of cases into Europe.

triage.headline_ja: 米国がエボラ患者発生国への便の運航停止をヨーロッパの首都に要求し、「一方的措置」で脅迫
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱の国際的拡大リスク、ヒト-ヒト感染の高い流行可能性、複数国での同時発生、および国際的渡航制限の可能性が存在する。IHR基準3項目以上該当。
triage.notes: DRCがエボラ患者の発生地として記事サマリーで明示されている。ウガンダ・ルワンダも言及されているが、対象国リストに含まれていないため除外。米国とベルギーは流行国ではなく、政策立案国として提示されているため除外。国際的な政治的・外交的関心が高く、渡航制限をめぐる国家間対立が生じている点が重要。フルRRA実施が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Fall in official Ebola numbers appears to be good news but it's not that simple
article.articleSummary: DR Congo Ebola outbreak concentrated in eastern provinces; 380 confirmed cases and 60 deaths in DR Congo, plus 15 confirmed cases and one death in neighboring Uganda. Earlier figures cited over 1,000 suspected cases and ~250 suspected deaths; current totals reflect confirmed diagnoses as labs rule out fever from malaria and other illnesses. WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus says the outbreak had a big head start but response teams are catching up. Major challenges include only ~45% of direct contacts followed up, hindered by conflict, and community mistrust, with a burial team attacked in South Kivu. The outbreak is caused by Bundibugyo Ebola, a rarer strain with no vaccine or proven treatment yet. WHO assesses risk as very high in DR Congo, high in the region, low globally; not airborne, though vaccines and therapies are under development, and trust-building and contact tracing are critical.

triage.headline_ja: 公式エボラ患者数の減少は朗報に見えるが、実はそれほど単純ではない
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4つ全て該当（深刻な公衆衛生影響、異常な病原体、国際的拡大、地域的懸念）。複数国での確認例、Bundibugyo株の希少性、接触追跡の低率、社会不安定性が懸念される。
triage.notes: ウガンダでの確認例（15例、1死亡）も記載されているが、ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations から除外。DRCは対象国（ID 203312）に含まれる。Bundibugyo株のワクチン・治療法不在、紛争・社会不安定性による対応困難、接触追跡低率（45%）が特に懸念される。WHO評価が「DRC内で非常に高リスク、地域で高リスク」であることも重要。

article.articleHeadline: Santé : L'OMS lance un plan de 518 millions de dollars pour enrayer l'épidémie d'Ebola Bundibugyo - LePotentiel
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Health: WHO launches a $518 million plan to curb the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak
article.articleSummary: {"description":"WHO launches a $518 million plan to curb the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda. The Bundibugyo ebolavirus (BDBV) outbreak was officially declared in the DRC on May 15, 2026, concentrated in Ituri province’s Rwampara, Mongbwalu and Bunia health zones; Uganda reported an imported case the same day, raising cross-border transmission concerns. BDBV has no approved vaccines or treatments, with past outbreaks showing case fatality rates of 30–50%. The response announced on June 5, 2026 rests on four pillars: (1) country-led action under “one plan, one budget, one team”; (2) concrete containment measures—including surveillance, rapid case finding, isolation and care, contact tracing, safe and dignified burials, and health-facility IPC; (3) a June–November 2026 execution timeline; (4) a $518 million funding package mobilizing WHO, Africa CDC and partners such as UNICEF, WFP, IFRC and FIND. Ongoing challenges include insecurity and access, but international and national engagement aims to contain spread and avert a larger humanitarian catastrophe."}

triage.headline_ja: 保健：WHO、ブンディブギョ・エボラウイルス流行を抑制するために5億1800万ドルの計画を開始
triage.triage_reason: エボラウイルス（BDBV）の国際的な流行事例であり、IHR基準の4項目すべてに該当。DRCおよびウガンダでの確認、高い致死率（30-50%）、国境を越えた感染リスク、WHOによる公式対応と多国間資金投資が明記されている。
triage.notes: 記事サマリーでウガンダ（輸入症例）も言及されているが、対象国リスト外のため verified_locations には含めない。Ituri州のMongbwalu、Bunia地区、Rwamparaが主要な感染地域。公式宣言は2026年5月15日。ブンディブギョエボラウイルス（BDBV）には承認ワクチン・治療法がなく、高い重症性を示す。

article.articleHeadline: ВОЗ: недоверие и дезинформация остаются одними из главных препятствий в борьбе со вспышкой Эболы в ДР Конго
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: WHO: mistrust and misinformation remain among the major obstacles in the fight against the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
article.articleSummary: As of June 3, 2026, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) totals 381 confirmed cases and 64 deaths, with Uganda reporting 15 confirmed and one probable case. WHO and Africa CDC launched a six‑month, $518 million plan to bolster outbreak response, including surveillance, diagnostics, clinical care, cross‑border collaboration, and risk communication. Laboratory capacity expanded from 40 to 800 tests per day, with most samples tested on receipt and results in 24–48 hours. Contact tracing coverage rose from about 25% to 45%, but the target remains 90–95%. A Congolese national who had traveled to the United Arab Emirates illustrates cross‑border risk. Mistrust persists: burial teams faced threats, and some locals attribute Ebola to witchcraft. WHO emphasizes culturally informed engagement with communities. Seven recoveries (six health workers) linked to early treatment. There is no vaccine or approved therapy for Bundibugyo ebolavirus yet; vaccine candidates may enter clinical trials in 4–6 months.

triage.headline_ja: WHO：ブンディブギョエボラウイルスとの戦いにおいて、不信と偽情報が主な障害のままである
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱の確認症例381件、死亡64件という重大な公衆衛生影響を伴う異常な感染症イベント。IHR基準において少なくとも3つ（深刻な影響、異常性、国際的拡大リスク）に該当し、複数国（DRC、ウガンダ）での感染と国際的な移動（UAE渡航者）が確認されている。
triage.notes: 発生地域にはUganda（226074）とUAE（290557）が含まれているが、対象国リスト内にはウガンダが明記されていないため verified_locations には DRC のみを記載した。サマリーからはウガンダでの15確認症例が報告されているが、評価対象国として指定されていないため除外とした。エボラ出血熱の性質上、確実にピックアップすべき高リスク事例である。

article.articleHeadline: Afrique: L'hôpital missionnaire Sainte-Thérèse lance une campagne de sensibilisation contre Ebola
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Africa: Sainte-Thérèse Mission Hospital launches an awareness campaign against Ebola.
article.articleSummary: Ebola awareness campaign launched by Sainte-Thérèse Mission Hospital in Nzara for the Tombura-Yambio Catholic Diocese to reinforce precautions against Ebola outbreaks now affecting the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda; South Sudan currently reports no confirmed cases. The June 4 awareness session at the Diocesan Curia highlighted regional public health concerns due to neighboring outbreaks, noting that South Sudan's Nzara has historical ties to Ebola, with the first outbreak in 1976 in Nzara county. Bishop Mgr Barani Eduardo Hiiboro Kussala thanked the hospital and CODEP for the initiative, stressing vigilance and the need for protective measures in daily life. He urged government authorities, international partners, communities, and scientists to intensify surveillance and multilingual education to reach all residents. The campaign involves diocese, Sainte-Thérèse Hospital, CODEP, Eve, priests, and Curia staff, aiming to prevent Ebola entry and safeguard Western Equatoria communities.

triage.headline_ja: アフリカ：サント・テレーズ・ミッション病院がエボラ出血熱対策啓発キャンペーンを実施
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱の地域的脅威認識と啓発活動の報告だが、南スーダンでの確認症例がなく、隣国（DRC・ウガンダ）の既知流行への対応段階。情報不足のため継続経過観察を要する。
triage.notes: 記事は南スーダンのNzaraにおける啓発キャンペーンを主題としているが、南スーダンは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations から除外。DRCの現在の流行が記事の文脈（隣国での既知流行に対する警戒）で言及されているため DRC のみ列挙。WPRO基準で prolonged_exposure (長期曝露リスク)・epidemic_prone (流行しやすさ)・manageability (外部支援ニーズ) が該当するが、南スーダンでの確認症例がなく、予防キャンペーン段階であるため WATCH とした。

article.articleHeadline: Duale: No Ebola in Kenya as 56 suspected cases test negative
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-06-05, Kenya reports no Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) cases as 56 suspected cases tested negative; in the last 24 hours 3,969 travelers were screened, bringing total screened since enhanced surveillance to over 80,000. All 56 samples from individuals with travel history to Uganda and the DRC tested negative. The country is strengthening defense against Bundibugyo strain seen in Uganda and DRC, with National Incident Management System activated, enhanced surveillance at airports, border posts, and four laboratories (National Public Health Laboratory, KEMRI Nairobi, KEMRI Kisumu, Busia mobile lab). 25 high-risk counties identified; 347 rapid response personnel on standby; 1,759 healthcare workers trained; simulations underway; public awareness campaigns for border communities, transport operators, healthcare workers. Officials urge vigilance, timely medical attention for Ebola-consistent symptoms (fever, headache, vomiting, diarrhea, fatigue). Emphasizes reliance on official information and ongoing regional surveillance amid cross-border movement from Uganda/DRC.

triage.headline_ja: ドゥアレ：ケニアではエボラは確認されず、56件の疑い事例がすべて陰性
triage.triage_reason: エボラウイルスの地域的な流行（ウガンダ・DRC）に隣接する国での強化された監視活動を示す。現在のケニアでは確認患者がなく、疑い事例が陰性であるが、高度な備態制がとられており、情報が限定的であるため経過観察が必要。
triage.notes: 記事の主題はケニアの防御体制強化を報じるものであり、実際のエボラ発症事例はケニアでは確認されていない。発生地域はウガンダおよびDRCであり、ケニアは隣接国として監視下にある。対象国リストではDRCのみが該当する。記事サマリー内でウガンダが言及されているが、対象国リストに含まれていないため、verified_locationsには含めない。ケニアは対象国リストに含まれていない。

article.articleHeadline: OMS lanza plan de USD 518 millones contra el ébola en África
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: WHO launches a USD 518 million plan to combat Ebola in Africa.
article.articleSummary: An Ebola outbreak declared May 15 in northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has escalated, with 381 confirmed cases and 64 deaths in DRC, and 16 cases (one death) in Uganda. Overall, at least 65 fatalities have occurred. The outbreak is driven by the Bundibugyo ebolavirus strain, with the Ituri province bearing the majority of cases (about 90%) and deaths (about 76%). Three provinces in the DRC are affected, centered in Ituri. On June 5, the WHO and Africa CDC unveiled a joint USD 518 million plan to combat the outbreak from June to November 2026, focusing on emergency coordination, surveillance, laboratory testing, infection prevention and control, clinical care, and community engagement. The current outbreak is larger than the Bundibugyo events in 2007 and 2012, underscoring its seriousness.

triage.headline_ja: WHO、アフリカでのエボラ出血熱対策に5億1800万ドルの計画を発表
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱の確認患者381名、死亡64名（DRC）、ウガンダでも16名の患者発生。IHR基準4項目すべてに該当し、WHOと各国政府が大規模な対応計画を策定していることから、フルRRAが必要。
triage.notes: 発生地域にはウガンダも含まれているが、対象国リストに該当しないため verified_locations には含めない。DRCは対象国として含める。記事サマリーからIturi州がDRCで感染の中心地であることが明記されており、規模・影響度から最優先のシグナルとして判定。

article.articleHeadline: فيروس "إيبولا" يشعل حالة طوارئ صحية دولية
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ebola virus triggers an international health emergency.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo reports 381 laboratory-confirmed cases and 63 deaths since its May 15 declaration, spanning Ituri, North Kivu, and South Kivu. About 233 people are in treatment or under monitoring in dedicated isolation centers. The outbreak is linked to Bundibugyo ebolavirus, a recognized Ebola strain, demanding precise responses in fragile health systems. Diagnostic capacity has surged after the arrival of over 4,000 testing kits from the African CDC and partners, enabling results in under 24 hours and speeding case isolation to curb transmission. The WHO has declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern; Africa CDC-led plan is coordinating cross-border response, surveillance, and early warning. Around 200 tons of medical supplies have been shipped, including about 80 tons to Bunia for field hospitals. Contact tracing has risen from 9% to 55%, with a target of 90%.

triage.headline_ja: エボラウイルスが国際的な保健上の緊急事態を引き起こしている
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱の大規模アウトブレイクであり、IHR基準4つすべてに該当。WHO Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC)宣言済みで、国際的な懸念と支援体制が機能している。
triage.notes: 2026年6月5日時点の記事。381例の確定患者、63死亡例を報告。Bundibugyo ebolavirus（エボラウイルス属の認定株）に関連。WHOがPHEIC宣言済み。アフリカCDC主導の対応が進行中。医療供給品約200トンが配送済み。接触追跡率が9%から55%に改善。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola: OMS e África CDC unem forças em plano continental de US$ 518 milhões
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola: WHO and Africa CDC join forces in a continent-wide plan worth US$518 million.
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo-strain Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Uganda triggers a continent-wide plan worth US$518 million to be executed June–November 2026. WHO and Africa CDC launched the Continental Plan for Ebola Preparedness and Response in Geneva. Cumulative figures: 906 suspected cases and 223 deaths since May across the two neighbors; alerts total 134, including 9 in Uganda with 18 validated deaths; 49 new confirmed cases reported. The plan is country-led, with a single budget and team, built on four premises: shared ownership, precise immediate actions, a six-month intensive window, and the stated budget. Partners include UNICEF, UNHCR, WFP, IFRC, and Findx. Core actions cover surveillance, diagnostics, IPC, clinical care, and logistics, with strong community engagement to combat misinformation. Real-time funding monitoring will track needs and gaps, protecting DRC, Uganda, and neighboring border regions.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ：WHOとアフリカCDCが5億1800万米ドルの大陸規模計画で連携
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準で4項目すべて該当（深刻な公衆衛生影響、予想外の多国間同時発生、国際的拡大リスク、渡航・貿易制限リスク）。Bundibugyo株エボラの多国家発生により、WPROスクリーニング基準も全項目該当。社会的・政治的関心も高い。フルRRA実施が必須。
triage.notes: 発生地域にはUganda（226074）も記載されているが、対象国リストに含まれていないため verified_locations から除外した。DRCとウガンダの国境地域での多国家エボラ発生。Bundibugyo株。WHOおよびアフリカCDCによる大規模な国際対応計画が発表されており、社会的・政治的関心は極めて高い。5月以降906疑似患者、223死亡という深刻な数字。

article.articleHeadline: WHO launches $518 million plan to curb Africa Ebola outbreak
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-06-05, WHO launches a $518 million six-month plan to curb an Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo and neighboring Uganda—the fourth largest on record. The Bundibugyo strain, with no approved treatment or vaccine, has caused 381 confirmed cases and 62 deaths in DRC, and 19 cases with 2 deaths in Uganda. The plan aims to contain spread in DRC and Uganda and bolster preparedness elsewhere through border screening and related measures. The outbreak was declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern after Congo's 17th outbreak was announced May 15. Testing has been challenging; some Ebola tests initially failed to detect Bundibugyo, and results can take days to a week. Mistrust and attacks on burial teams and treatment centers hinder response. Security support includes three armoured UN vehicles; donors have pledged $315.8 million (down from $498 million) for the response.

triage.headline_ja: WHO、アフリカのエボラ出血熱拡大抑止に5億1,800万ドルの計画を発動
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準において4項目すべてに該当。コンゴ民主共和国およびウガンダでのエボラ出血熱（ブンディブギョ株）の拡大により、深刻な公衆衛生上の影響、異常性、国際的拡大リスク、および渡航・貿易制限リスクが存在。WHO公式発表による国際的関心も極めて高い。
triage.notes: 記事サマリーに基づき、実際のイベント発生地はコンゴ民主共和国とウガンダ。対象国リストではDRC（203312）のみ該当。ウガンダは対象国外。ブンディブギョ株は治療法・ワクチンなく、検査の課題と住民の不信が対応を複雑化させている。PHEIC宣言済みで国際的対応が進行中。

article.articleHeadline: Why Ebola Is Proving Hard to Slow in Congo
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-06-05, Ebola, one of the deadliest diseases with a fatality rate as high as 90%, remains extraordinarily difficult to slow. An outbreak in northeastern Democratic Republic of Congo has spread to neighboring Uganda, illustrating cross-border transmission and the ongoing containment challenge. Governments treat Ebola as a national-security threat given its severity and potential impact on health systems. The article highlights how cross-border movement and the virus’s lethality complicate response efforts, requiring vigilance beyond a single country. With transmission extending beyond its origin, the outbreak underscores the international dimensions of Ebola control and the persistent hurdles to stopping new cases in areas with varied healthcare resources.
